land.text: the eastern half of the Moghul khanate: 'in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan'

predecessors.note: The chagatai-khanate dossier ends in 1462 and lists only moghulistan as successor; this row is the other half.

land.text: the Tarim Basin and Turfan joined to the western khanate by Yunus Khan

successors.note: 'After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate' (Moghulistan page).

capitals.name: Aksu
capitals.note: Yunus Khan page on Dost Muhammad: 'took up residence in the town of Aksu'; Esen Buqa II page: 'The khan moved to Aksu' during a period of disorder (undated).

keyframe_review.note: 1,080,075 km2 for 1463-1467 (73.6-92.7E, 35.4-45.3N; the gazetteer measures 952,000 km2): the Tarim Basin and Turfan. The page named as Cliopatria's Wikipedia title, East Turkestan, is a modern-region article and has nothing on the 15th century; the Esen Buqa II page gives 'in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan' without an outline, and the Yunus Khan page 'the settled lands of Eastern Moghulistan (Uyghurstan)'. The pages give no area; the Tarim Basin region alone measures about 940,000 km2 by the gazetteer, so the figure is plausible.

1,079,785 km2. Valid for 1468-1469 only: 'After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate' (Moghulistan page); the Yunus Khan page: Dost died 'in 1468 or 1469, after which Yunus seized Aksu'. From 1470 the same land is drawn in moghulistan_1470. region.text: the settled lands of Eastern Moghulistan (Uyghurstan): the Tarim Basin and Turfan

ledger.note: 1463: Dost Muhammad holds the east. 'in the east Esen Buqa's son Dost Muhammad became khan' on his father's death in 1462; he 'consolidated his hold on all settled lands in Eastern Moghulistan, known at the time as Uyghurstan' and 'took up residence in the town of Aksu' (Yunus Khan page). The dossier starts in 1463, Cliopatria's year, because the chagatai-khanate dossier ends in 1462.

1469: Dost Muhammad dies and Yunus Khan reunites the khanate. 'After the death of Dost Muhammad in 1469, Yunus Khan reunited the khanate' (the Yunus Khan page has 'in 1468 or 1469, after which Yunus seized Aksu'); the reunion has no date of its own, and Cliopatria draws the East Turkestan row to 1474.

wars.name: Moghul succession war after Esen Buqa II (1462-1469)
wars.outcome: The khanate divided in 1462 between Dost Muhammad in the east and Yunus Khan in the west; Dost died in 1468 or 1469 and Yunus reunited the khanate, seizing Aksu.
wars.note: The Moghulistan page: 'When Esen Buqa died in 1462, the Dughlat amirs split between his son Dost Muhammad and his brother Yunus Khan.'

certainty.note: Oasis polity of the Tarim and Turfan; no page gives a frontier.

notes:
Written for batch ia-02-d. Four pages opened (budget 1-2 for 2 shapes; three of the four are shared with moghulistan). The page named in Cliopatria's row, East Turkestan, is a modern-region article and covers neither 1463-1474 nor a state.
Decision on the shared Wikidata id (Q840601, 'East Turkestan' / 'East Turkestan Republic'): different states. The row of 1463-1474 is the eastern half of the divided Moghul khanate, Dost Muhammad's khanate (the Tarim Basin and Turfan, seat at Aksu); the East Turkestan Republic of 1945-1949 is a 20th-century republic that merely shares the regional name. Not merged; east-turkestan-republic is owned elsewhere.
Reading: the Esen Buqa II page splits the realm in 1462 between Yunus (west) and Dost Muhammad (east); Cliopatria's Moghulistan 1463-1474 row is the west and East Turkestan 1463-1474 the east, and Moghulistan's 1475 shape is exactly the sum of the two 1468 shapes (3 and 2 cells of difference). The pages name no outline for Dost's khanate; the Cliopatria shape stands for 'the settled lands of Eastern Moghulistan (Uyghurstan)'.
Corrected: the life ends in 1469 (Dost's death, reunion afterwards) instead of 1474; east-turkestan_1468 is valid 1468-1469 only and moghulistan_1470 carries the land from 1470.
Unsettled: the date of Dost Muhammad's death (1468 or 1469 on the Yunus page, 1469 on the Moghulistan page); when Dost's reign began beyond the 1462 succession; the Dughlat amirs (Mirza Abu Bakr at Kashgar) held parts of the Tarim in these years, which no page opened dates; Ming and Oirat relations of Hami and Turfan are not recorded (the Ming is a seed neighbour 1463-1467).
Not opened: Dost Muhammad Khan (if there is a page), Dughlat, Mirza Abu Bakr Dughlat, Aksu.
Gazetteer: nothing missing.
